title: IO Graph: prevent crashes due to missing null checks
description:
Add additional NULL checks to prevent crashes.

Crashes occur for example when closing the io graph while it is plotting
because updateLegend event gets called after ressources are freed and the
dialog is already closed.

notes.body:
ui not being initialized would mean, that we are being called on a private object (not initiated through the original constructor) and therefore something else is going seriously wrong. Can you provide a path of replication for this issue?

I would much rather remove the underlying cause as otherwise we would just keep on updating backends until all cracks are filled, instead of fixing the initial leak to begin with.

Also, would it be not enough to check for ui != NULL inside updateLegend and prevent it being used if it is not present?

IO Graph crashes quite often when I use it. It typically crashes when I change settings during a rescan. But I was not able to find a specific scenario to reproduce it.

The only crash that I was able to reproduce in a reliable way was when you hit close while the rescan is performed. (Using a large trace file is recommended) In this case the crash is caused by member `ui` being `NULL`. That's why I assume that other crashes may have the same root cause.

I think `ui` becomes NULL because of a race condition during closing the IO Graph.

My opinion: In general pointers should be checked for NULL before they are used.

> I think `ui` becomes NULL because of a race condition during closing the IO Graph.
> 
> My opinion: In general pointers should be checked for NULL before they are used.

My opinion: In general, race conditions should be fixed; if Wireshark behaves differently depending on how fast thread A advances relative to thread B, that's a bug.

Hm. The underlying root-cause is something else. The crash occurs, because of a dataChanged event in the uatModel. The reason why this is happening is the redissection. So far so good. The problem here is, that we emit way to many dataChanged events in the UatModel. Namely each for each field of the list of graphs. Which is also, what makes reloading the graphs way slower than they should be.

So what happens? The list of graphs is based on UatModel. And UatModel seems to have a significant design flaw. When you add new lines to it, it assumes that the line gets created by the owner of the model and then populated by the owner using setData, which will trigger a signal every single time it is called. Therefore the View will get updated every time you add an entry. That by itself is bad. But the real issue here is the way UatModels seem to add lines to it. It is completely bogus to insert the row and then let the owner of the model populate.  That is exactly the opposite of how models work in the first place. And it removes all necessities for the model/view concept. It is however, how the underlying system is supposed to work. There seems to have been an effort to port the underlying model to a movel/view class, but not with the full grasp of the model/view concept.

So why does the crash occur? Well, when you close the dialog and a redissect is happening, this redissection is being signaled through CaptureFile, a Qt class managing the capture file signaling in a single place. That is fine, except for the fact, that IoGraphDialog is not the owner of the CaptureFile instance, MainWindow is. So closing the dialog, does not stop the redissection issuing signals per se (except in the deconstructor, where we tell the redissection to stop). So even if closing immediately shuts off the signaling system for IoGraph and all it's children, the UatModel still get's updated, as this is handled via the dataChanged signals emitted by CaptureFile. The Model then triggers the View (which at this point should not happen, but can in rare cases, if the deconstructor has not run yet), and voila - we crash.

An easy solution would be to indeed safeguard the UI element, but this actually is a bandage at best, not really a solution. A better one would be to guard dataChanged. The real solution is two-fold. First, the way new lines are being inserted into UatModel has to change. This is a perverted approach and it needs to be cleaned up. The second is, we need to be aware of closing the model, and ensure that when we are already closing, all events being fired will be return without action. This too is a bandage like solution, but it is the correct one.

I've added a merge request (!4135) to fix the issue with the multiple signals and I am no longer able to reproduce the crash. @Developer-Alexander may I ask that you try this change and see if it fixes it for you too?

I made some quick tests with !4135. (As mentioned earlier I have no reliable way to reproduce crashes.)

I got **no crash** when closing the IO Graph.

I got a crash when removing a graph:

`(wireshark:11856) 17:31:07.895644 [GUI ERROR] -- ASSERT failure in QVector<T>::operator[]: "index out of range", file D:\Dev\wireshark_dependencies\qt_5.15\msvc2019_64\include\QtCore/qvector.h, line 463`
![image](/uploads/407ca4b25d12a72167ff11b5b07fe4e7/image.png)

And I noticed that not all changes are taken when I change setting during a rescan. For example when I change the interval or when I change from MAX to MIN of a Y Field. The rescan goes on but the chart freezes. It only recovers when I make a change that triggers a new rescan.
Found it. Well, that was a small thing with a big outcome. I will close this issue, as the other merge request has the solution to the underlying cause.
